aboutParagraphs: I am a Frontend / Software Engineer with 6+ years of experience building production React, Next.js, and TypeScript applications across enterprise software, ERP, and fintech.

The work is not limited to UI. It includes frontend architecture, HTTP/API contracts, backend integration, data-heavy interfaces, authentication and role-based access control, complex CRUD workflows, large-scale migrations, production debugging, and end-to-end ownership of frontend features. English C1. Available for remote full-time and project roles as a Frontend Engineer, Senior Frontend Developer, React Engineer, Next.js Engineer, or Software Engineer.

enterpriseErp.name: Enterprise ERP Frontend
enterpriseErp.whatItIs: Production multi-module ERP · Next.js · TypeScript · REST API
enterpriseErp.description: A large production ERP frontend spanning Finance, Warehouse, HR, Projects, Tasks, office/document workflows, Users, Roles, Permissions, and Self-service. Warehouse covers 16+ operational areas; HR includes 20+ sections of the employee dossier. The system is data-heavy: server pagination, filtering, sorting, URL state, and permissioned CRUD.
enterpriseErp.contribution: Led the frontend migration from a legacy UI/API architecture to Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui, and TanStack — covering both UI and API/data-contract work. Built production interfaces with TanStack Table, TanStack Query, React Hook Form, Zod, RBAC, authentication, sessions, and file uploads, while removing legacy dependencies without stopping the running application. Audited Finance HTTP contracts (13/13 domains), resolved a production routing regression that could send ERP traffic to the legacy Nest backend, and reworked localization into a centralized system.
enterpriseErp.whyItMatters: Shows frontend architecture and API-contract ownership on an enterprise ERP: MUI-zero / DataGrid-zero migration gates, 46 incorrect Finance contracts and 8 P0 issues found before cutover, and regression suites that reached 710 passing tests.

spy.name: Spy Game — offline-first app
spy.whatItIs: Interactive web app · offline-first · client-side logic
spy.description: A mobile interactive app without backend or registration: players pass one phone around, reveal their cards, discuss clues and vote. Game logic, timer, word database and progress persistence run fully on the client.
spy.contribution: Implemented the full client-side loop: setup, role generation, pass-the-phone UX, Classic/Hardcore modes, 3D flip-card animation, discussion timer, voting, custom word database with JSON import/export and localStorage persistence with SSR-safe hydration.
spy.whyItMatters: Shows how I design game loops, private state, mobile-first UX and reliable flows without backend dependencies.

bunker.name: Bunker — realtime multiplayer app
bunker.description: A realtime multiplayer app with rooms, host/player roles and hidden character cards. The host imports an AI-generated scenario and manages rounds, events, voting and the final story.
bunker.contribution: Designed a Firestore room model with realtime subscriptions, separate host/player screens and a full game FSM. Private card fields remain hidden from other players until revealed, while the public game state is synchronized in realtime across the room. AI-friendly workflow: prompt → scenario → parser → validation → play.
bunker.whyItMatters: Demonstrates realtime multiplayer, game state machines, private/public state modeling and AI-friendly scenario import without an over-engineered backend.

tWhale.name: T-Whale
tWhale.description: A Telegram WebApp game with progression mechanics and chat-native user journeys. The product focuses on retention and repeat sessions inside the Telegram ecosystem.
tWhale.contribution: Frontend functionality, user flows and integration-facing parts of the Telegram WebApp experience: progression screens, state handling and coordination with bot/backend logic.
tWhale.whyItMatters: Demonstrates practical delivery in Telegram ecosystem products with real interaction loops.

web3Fintech.name: Web3 / Fintech / AML Flows
web3Fintech.description: Frontend flows for products involving wallets, transactions and compliance checks. The focus is safe UX around finance-sensitive operations.
web3Fintech.contribution: Wallet connections (WalletConnect, TronLink), balances, transactions and token approve for Tron/Ethereum, plus AML/blockchain checks integrated into frontend flows.
web3Fintech.whyItMatters: Shows applied experience with finance-sensitive and blockchain-integrated user journeys.

nova.name: Nova Engineering ERP
nova.whatItIs: Public demo ERP · industrial automation · ICS / SCADA / MES
nova.description: A public demo ERP for an engineering company: 10 modules with role-based access (7 roles), a dashboard with metrics and charts, CRUD tables on MUI X DataGrid with server-side pagination, sorting, filtering and search, plus i18n RU/EN. This is a demonstration product, separate from the production ERP case above.
nova.contribution: Architecture on Feature-Sliced Design with a switchable data layer: one contract, two implementations — a mock backend (seed + localStorage) and a real REST API with no UI changes. Role-based access, project and equipment accounting, certificates and report export, SSR CSS-in-JS without hydration errors.
nova.whyItMatters: A public reference for enterprise frontend architecture: RBAC, CRUD tables, and a switchable REST data layer rather than a marketing page.

itdealgroup.name: ITDEAL — company website
itdealgroup.description: Production website of ITDEAL (Chisinau): the studio ships CRM/ERP, Telegram bots, AI and blockchain products. The site covers services, a 4-step delivery process, a filterable case catalog and a lead form, with RU/EN.
itdealgroup.contribution: Frontend work on the company site, mainly the cases section: card layout, category filters, load-more, responsive UI and clearer navigation across commercial projects.
itdealgroup.whyItMatters: A live B2B marketing site with a real case catalog, not a template landing.

trustpay.name: TrustPay
trustpay.description: A fintech frontend from the Itdeal period: payment-oriented screens and API-facing UI around payment scenarios. The original public URL no longer resolves, so there is no live demo at the moment.
trustpay.contribution: Public-facing frontend: screen structure, responsive layout and UI around payment and API scenarios.
trustpay.whyItMatters: Commercial fintech UI work in a payment product — the case stays in the portfolio even though the demo is offline.

dezv3.name: WorkDez — disinfection field app
dezv3.whatItIs: Field-service app · Telegram WebApp · order workflow
dezv3.description: WorkDez is an aggregator for disinfection technicians across Russia: incoming orders, a task queue (call the client, start, report, pay, complete), wallet and average check, work schedule, ratings and phone-number auth. Runs as a mobile web app and a Telegram WebApp.
dezv3.contribution: Frontend of the master app: signup/login, task list and order actions, wallet/balance, schedule, Telegram WebApp shell and Firebase Hosting deploy.
dezv3.whyItMatters: A real operations product: field workflows, money-related UI and Telegram-native delivery — not a marketing page.

mosca.name: Bitex — OTC USDT exchange
mosca.whatItIs: Telegram WebApp · cash RUB ↔ USDT · AML
mosca.description: OTC desk in Moscow: buy/sell USDT for cash rubles, 24/7, table-to-table (no custody of client funds), live rate, orders, AML check, referral program and office-pass flow via the bot.
mosca.contribution: Frontend of the Telegram WebApp: home, swap, rate, orders, about, AML and referral screens on React/MUI, with Telegram Web Apps integration and Firebase Hosting.
mosca.whyItMatters: A live fintech WebApp with compliance (AML) and transactional UX, not a landing.

aviaLanding.name: avia-landing.vercel.app
aviaLanding.description: A landing page for presenting the service and capturing user interest. The focus was clean responsive UI, fast loading, clear content structure and production deployment.
aviaLanding.contribution: Page structure, visual composition, responsive layout and preparation for public Vercel deployment.
aviaLanding.whyItMatters: Complements product work with polished landing execution and deploy-ready frontend.

telegramBots.name: Telegram Bot References
telegramBots.description: Supporting bot-side references connected to Telegram workflows.
telegramBots.contribution: Built and maintained bot-related functionality for project use and testing scenarios.
telegramBots.whyItMatters: Demonstrates practical understanding of Telegram product ecosystem beyond UI-only scope.

experience.scope: Led frontend migration of a production ERP from a legacy UI/API architecture, including both interface work and HTTP/data-contract migration across major business modules, without stopping the running application.
points: Migrated Warehouse, HR, Projects, Tasks, Users, roles and permissions, office/document workflows, Finance, and Self-service to the new ERP API. Warehouse covers 16+ operational areas; HR includes 20+ sections of the employee dossier.
Eliminated a large legacy UI surface: started at 135 MUI importers, 59 MUI icon importers, and 31 DataGrid files; migration gates reached MUI-zero and DataGrid-zero.

Audited 13/13 Finance domains (invoices, estimates, payments, expenses, recurring operations, reports, transactions): identified 46 incorrect frontend API contracts, 22 missing scenarios, and 8 P0 issues before production cutover.

Integrated against NestJS APIs backed by Prisma and PostgreSQL — request/response models, frontend data models, RBAC, authentication, sessions, file uploads, server pagination, filtering, sorting, and URL state.
Reworked localization as architecture: moved about 420 hardcoded UI strings into 22 namespaces and 951 translation keys, and removed legacy i18next dependencies.
Resolved a production routing regression where ERP requests could fall back to the legacy Nest backend when ERP URL configuration was invalid, and added configuration safeguards.
Migration stages passed regression gates: a controlled milestone at 682 tests across 160 files with typecheck, build, and API-contract checks; later the suite reached 710 passing tests.

Implemented Web3 wallet UX with WalletConnect and TronLink: balances, transactions, and token approvals on Tron/Ethereum.
Integrated AML and blockchain checks into frontend journeys with backend data transfer.
Refactored legacy frontend modules to reduce technical debt and stabilize architecture.

Supported event-related IT operations and delegate coordination.

Worked with React and participated in migration from class components to functional patterns.
Contributed to integrations involving Hasura, Docker, basic TypeScript, and GraphQL.
